definition: Two complex numbers $a + b\mathrm{i}$ and $a - b\mathrm{i}$, with $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $b \ne 0$: each is the complex conjugate of the other.
For an integer $n$, $\left[r(\cos\theta + \mathrm{i}\sin\theta)\right]^{n} = r^{n}(\cos n\theta + \mathrm{i}\sin n\theta)$: raise the modulus to the power $n$ and multiply the argument by $n$.
The $n$ solutions of $z^{n} = 1$, which are $\mathrm{cis}\,\frac{2\pi k}{n}$ for $k = 0, 1, \ldots, n - 1$.
